results.title: One of the major highlights of the NACCIMA B2B Investment Forum in Guanghzou, China was the presentation of specific projects and investment
results.description:
One of the major highlights of the NACCIMA B2B Investment Forum in Guanghzou, China was the presentation of specific projects and investment proposals by the Nigerian delegates to attract partnership, support, and technical collaboration from interested Chinese investors.

Vice Chancellor of the University of Ilorin (UNILORIN), Prof. Wahab Olasupo Egbewole, SAN, made a compelling case for partnership and investment in the institution, showcasing its huge potential in agriculture, industrial park, power generation, and others.

Similarly, Arc. Zakirudeen Oladotun of Infrabridge Advisory Development Limited lined up a number of projects in need of technical and financial partnership for their actualisation, calling on the Chinese investors to take keen interest in them as the Return on Investment (RoI) are projected to be high.

Other investment presentations came from representatives of Alaro City, Lekki Worldwide Investments Ltd, and Nigerian Office for Trade Negotiations.

The @NACCIMA30 B2B event provided a platform for solid partnership, collaboration, and networking between key players and business leaders in both Nigeria and China.

#NACCIMAB2BForum
#UNILORIN
#Infrabridge

results.title: 2/11. We will sign a Build-Operate-Transfer deal with a Chinese state company on day one. China Export-Import Bank pays 70% of the cost. Fed
results.description:
2/11. We will sign a Build-Operate-Transfer deal with a Chinese state company on day one. China Export-Import Bank pays 70% of the cost. Federal Government pays 30%. 

Chinese companies build and run the plants for some years, then hand them over fully to Nigeria. We use Nigerian workers for civil works, roads, fencing, and simpler installation jobs.

results.title: The best-selling phone brand in Africa was built around a selfie problem.
results.description:
The best-selling phone brand in Africa was built around a selfie problem.

Samsung and Nokia had the famous brands. A Chinese company almost unknown at home took the market. Here's how listening beat branding.

Transsion is based in Shenzhen.
It started selling phones in Nigeria in the mid-2000s, under the name Tecno.

At the time, Nokia and Samsung owned the African phone market.

Transsion did not try to out-advertise them.
It studied how people actually used their phones.

↳ People carried two SIM cards to avoid network fees and patchy coverage, but few could afford two phones. Transsion sold dual-SIM phones in 2008, two years before Nokia did.
↳ Power cuts were common, so batteries had to last.
↳ And the front camera was the first thing many buyers checked in the shop.

Most phone cameras were tuned on lighter skin.
On darker skin, especially in low light, faces came out dark and unclear.

Transsion analysed several million photos of dark-skinned Africans.
Its cameras find the face using the eyes and teeth, then add the right amount of exposure.

The result:
In 2017, Transsion overtook Samsung as Africa's number one phone supplier.
In 2024, it held 49% of Africa's smartphone market and became the world's fourth largest smartphone seller, shipping 106.7 million units.

Here's my read:

Transsion did not win with a better spec sheet. It won by treating a problem every global brand ignored as the main feature. In a new market, the gap your competitors cannot see is often the whole strategy.

1. Watch the shop counter, not the spec sheet.
What buyers check first tells you what they value. For Transsion's buyers, it was the selfie camera.

2. Local problems are product requirements.
Two SIMs, weak power, low light. None of these were edge cases there. They were daily life.

3. Usefulness builds the brand.
Nokia had decades of trust in Africa. It lost to a brand that solved daily problems better.

The short version: global brands assume the product travels.
The winners rebuild it around the people using it.

This is how we try to think at OrbitX.

What works for us in Dubai does not get copied into Nigeria.
↳ In Nigeria, we lead with receiving money from abroad: US clients and family overseas send to a USD account as a local transfer, and the money is then withdrawn into a local NGN account.
↳ We are working on mobile payments next, because that is how people there want to pay.

We build for how the market moves money, not how we wish it did.

What is one local problem in your market that global brands still treat as an edge case?

#GlobalExpansion #Africa #Fintech

results.title: Both projects began under Buhari.
results.description:
Both projects began under Buhari. Kaduna-Kano (CCECC) was planned with China Exim funding that later withdrew; China Development Bank provided a ~$255m tranche in 2025 (China ~85%, Nigeria 15%). It stood at roughly 15-30% complete in May 2023 and is now near 90%. 

Kano-Katsina-Maradi (Mota-Engil) used mixed DFI funding including AfDB, DBSA and a later $1.8bn package; it was about 5% complete in 2023 and is now ~70%. 

Tinubu’s role has been releasing counterpart funds, securing the renewed Chinese financing, resolving land issues and accelerating remaining works toward the December 2026 sections.

results.title: TVC NEWS REPORT: FROM GUANGHZOU TO HAINAN, NACCIMA IS CONNECTING NIGERIA'S PRIVATE SECTOR TO INTERNATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES AND PARTNERSHIPS Ni
results.description:
TVC NEWS REPORT: FROM GUANGHZOU TO HAINAN, NACCIMA IS CONNECTING NIGERIA'S PRIVATE SECTOR TO INTERNATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES AND PARTNERSHIPS

Nigeria was well represented at the recently concluded 2026 Hainan Free Trade Port International Investment Cooperation Promotion Conference that was held in Haikou between November 4th and 6th.

Leading the Nigerian delegation to the high-level event after the successful @NACCIMA30 B2B Investment Forum in Guangzhou were the National President NACCIMA, Engr. Jani Ibrahim, mni, OON, and the Consul General of Nigeria in Guangzhou, Amb. Mairo Musa Abbas.

The conference exposed delegates to the many opportunities available in the Hainan free trade port including the many favourable government policies such as zero tariff, tax reduction, special customs operations, among other incentives that encourage exports, cross-border trade, investments, and international partnerships.

In this TVC news report, more details are provided on the deliberations at the important engagement.

results.title: Emmanuel Faith Mba, from Ohafia LGA of Abia State, has made Nigeria proud after emerging as the National Champion of the 2026 Nigerian Chine
results.description:
Emmanuel Faith Mba, from Ohafia LGA of Abia State, has made Nigeria proud after emerging as the National Champion of the 2026 Nigerian Chinese Bridge Competition and winning the Global Third Prize in China.

Despite learning Chinese for just 18 months, she competed against 157 contestants from 138 countries, earning a place among the Global Top 30.

Her achievement has earned commendation from the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria and brought pride to Ohafia, Abia State and Ndi Igbo in general 🔥

results.title: Just in case you're wondering what's going on, China cars are already close to the verge of dominating the car space.
results.description:
Just in case you're wondering what's going on, China cars are already close to the verge of dominating the car space. Their cars are cheap and smart.

In this post, I've made a list of 7 legit and reliable sites where you can get China cars at low costs. Two of them are run by NYSE-listed companies. The rest are smaller export agents, so check them before you pay.

1. AutoCango (https://t.co/s78avyxWSy): Over 2 million used cars plus new ones. Backed by a NYSE-listed parent company. Third-party inspection reports come in English.

2. China EV Marketplace (https://t.co/GvgJ37sFH5): Electric cars only, new and used. BYD, Xiaomi, Zeekr and more. 20% deposit, balance after you confirm the VIN and photos.

3. Autohome Global (https://t.co/vKyDggsypp): Run by Autohome Inc., also NYSE-listed. They say your payment is held until the car ships, with a refund if it doesn't arrive.

4. ZEEX AUTO (https://t.co/uUVu7VPQgW): Inspect first, pay later. A third-party inspection costs $100 and you approve the report before paying for the car. They also have an Africa site, https://t.co/hPZANs31ci.

5. EAuto Export (https://t.co/bhQ1jgDWUs): A sourcing agent in Beijing. Over 100,000 listings and independent on-site inspection. Fee is 3% of the car price, minimum $600.

6. Auto In China (https://t.co/baqk5mxJrH): A sourcing agent in Guangzhou. Good for ready-stock cars, luxury brands and EVs. Fee for one car is 7% of the price, minimum $300 and maximum $400.

7. Guazi (https://t.co/cSj3HUY5Co): Used cars only. Daily auctions or Buy It Now. Every car gets a 200-point inspection and a grade from S to D.

Before you pay for any car:

- Nigeria only accepts left-hand drive. Check this first.

- Used cars have an age limit. Confirm the current one with Customs before you buy.

- The listed price is FOB, the price at the Chinese port. Shipping, duty and clearing come on top.

- Ask for the inspection report. For EVs, ask for the battery report too. Chinese EVs use GB/T chargers.

- Pay a company account against a signed contract. Never a personal account.
